chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The one who flees from two men during the fighting in the advance (al-zahf) has fled (retreated), and the one who flees from three men during the fighting in the advance has not fled (has not retreated).'

key_terms.الزَّحْفِ: The advance or forward movement of troops in battle

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal distinction between fleeing from two versus three soldiers in battle?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the jurisprudential criteria for distinguishing between a valid tactical regrouping and a culpable retreat (fawr) in Shia military law, specifically noting that fleeing from two opponents constitutes a full retreat, whereas fleeing from three is not. This ruling reflects the practical realities of early Islamic warfare, where maintaining formation against a superior force was often a strategic necessity rather than cowardice. It underscores the importance of context in evaluating a soldier's conduct during the Zuhf (the initial phase of battle).
